author_or_org: Kowshik Chowdhury, Dipayan Banik, K M Ferdous, Shazibul Islam Shamim

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The study analyzes 3,109 unique pull requests from AIDev's 19,450 PRs in the commented review state, comparing human-only and CRA-only reviews.
claims.quote: From AIDev's 19,450 PRs, we analyze 3,109 unique PRs in the commented review state, comparing human-only versus CRA-only reviews.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: CRA-only pull requests have a 45.20% merge rate, which is 23.17 percentage points lower than human-only pull requests at 68.37%, and they show significantly higher abandonment.
claims.quote: CRA-only PRs achieve a 45.20% merge rate, 23.17 percentage points lower than human-only PRs (68.37%), with significantly higher abandonment.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The authors examine 98 closed CRA-only pull requests to assess whether low signal-to-noise ratios contribute to abandonment.
claims.quote: We examine 98 closed CRA-only PRs to assess whether low signal-to-noise ratios contribute to abandonment.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: In signal-to-noise analysis, 60.2% of closed CRA-only PRs fall into the 0-30% signal range, and 12 of 13 CRAs have average signal ratios below 60%, indicating substantial noise in automated review feedback.
claims.quote: Our signal-to-noise analysis reveals that 60.2% of closed CRA-only PRs fall into the 0-30% signal range, and 12 of 13 CRAs exhibit average signal ratios below 60%, indicating substantial noise in automated review feedback.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The findings suggest that CRAs without human oversight often generate low-signal feedback associated with higher abandonment.
claims.quote: These findings suggest that CRAs without human oversight often generate low-signal feedback associated with higher abandonment.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper advises practitioners that CRAs should augment rather than replace human reviewers, and that human involvement remains critical for effective and actionable code review.
claims.quote: For practitioners, our results indicate that CRAs should augment rather than replace human reviewers and that human involvement remains critical for effective and actionable code review.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Industry reports claim that CRAs can manage 80% of pull requests in open source repositories without human involvement.
claims.quote: Industry reports claim that CRAs can manage 80% of PRs in open source repositories without human involvement.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Autonomous coding agents are generating code at scale, with OpenAI Codex alone creating over 400,000 pull requests in two months.
claims.quote: Autonomous coding agents are generating code at an unprecedented scale, with OpenAI Codex alone creating over 400,000 pull requests (PRs) in two months.
